A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CompactFusion work and are readable throughout, including figures, tables, equations and appendices. Existing material can be matched despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video quality and latency measurements, component ablations, network experiments and a human evaluation with 20 valid responses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds CogVideoX temporal-stability measurements in Appendix F.5, Table 7.

M1.justification: Residual compression, error feedback, quantization, low-rank compression and system integration remain unchanged. Added pseudocode explains existing parallelism strategies rather than introducing a new CompactFusion component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO image prompts, VBench video prompts, FLUX.1-dev, CogVideoX-2b and the same hardware/network coverage. The added temporal metrics concern the existing six-GPU CogVideoX setting, without a new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged, including image-only PipeFusion evaluation. The new temporal table uses the already-evaluated uncompressed reference and DistriFusion; the added background pseudocode does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F.5 adds VBench Temporal Flickering and Motion Smoothness metrics for six-GPU CogVideoX evaluation. Existing sample counts, inference steps, warmups, hardware settings and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The rank-versus-precision, error-feedback, warmup and bandwidth analyses are retained unchanged. Table 7 adds aggregate video-quality metrics rather than a distinct ablation, perturbation, sensitivity test or case analysis.

E5.justification: v2 introduces no new repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 7 reports point scores, and the existing human-study sample information is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and existing qualitative examples retain their results. New Table 7 reports flickering/smoothness scores of 0.9644/0.9808 for Compact-2bit versus 0.9658/0.9795 for DistriFusion, alongside uncompressed, 1-bit and low-rank results.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 and the assumptions, bounds and proofs in v1 Appendix G/v2 Appendix H are retained. The additional equality in the residual-error proof merely substitutes the already-defined activation recurrence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about compression, fidelity, speedups and integration. The additional temporal evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F.5 newly interprets the temporal scores as showing comparable stability and no noticeable degradation from compression. Existing mechanism explanations, practical limitations and qualifications of the theoretical analysis remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies illustrative Patch Parallel/Ring Attention pseudocode and expands implementation documentation about residual-base updates, sender-side error feedback and communication wrappers. These clarify existing procedures; compression parameters, hardware disclosures and code access are unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists and novelty positioning are unchanged. Appendix B explains already-cited parallelism strategies more fully without adding literature or changing the claimed relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a More Preliminaries appendix and short implementation explanations, relocates and expands acknowledgments, and updates author/venue text and cross-references. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Patch Parallel Figure 9, two pseudocode displays and temporal-stability Table 7. Existing visual results are retained, with limited resizing, relocation and renumbering; the front-page layout also changes.

improvement.justification: The temporal metrics address a video-quality aspect not directly measured in v1, while the added parallelism and implementation explanations improve clarity. These are limited gains: core results and theory remain unchanged, and point scores without uncertainty or temporal perceptual testing do not fully substantiate the new claim of no noticeable degradation.
